verdict: Shopify: Choose Shopify when you want the default hosted ecommerce platform — fast launch, strong checkout, channels, and a proven scale path. Scores use the Ecommerce editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Best-in-class hosted storefront + checkout bundle for most DTC brands
Strong POS and payments story for omnichannel
weaknesses: TCO rises with apps, themes, and non-Shopify Payments
Advanced customization can require dev help
bestFor: Merchants wanting a hosted store without managing infrastructure
Brands scaling across online + retail channels
Teams that value app ecosystem over building custom stacks
notIdealFor: Merchants who need full code ownership on day one with zero subscription
Pure dropshipping-only workflows with no storefront ambition
Buyers optimizing solely for lowest processing spread at tiny volume
tradeoffs: Subscription floors vs payment-processing spreads and GMV/overage fees
App/extension TCO vs native feature depth
Open-source/hosting flexibility vs SaaS operational simplicity
Dropshipping product caps vs catalog automation depth
recommendation: Choose Shopify when you want the default hosted ecommerce platform — fast launch, strong checkout, channels, and a proven scale path. Consider BigCommerce for multi-storefront GMV packaging; WooCommerce for WordPress/open-source control; Square Online if in-person POS is the center of gravity.
editorialNotes: Ecommerce Wave-1 batch. Approved on ecommerce-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=saas-platform. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Shopify’s guided admin, theme editor, and app ecosystem let most merchants launch without developers — scored from first-party positioning, not hands-on lab testing.
Primary job is hosted ecommerce — storefront, catalog, checkout, and channels are core product surfaces, not bolt-ons.
Variants, inventory locations, orders, and fulfillment workflows scale to mid-market and Plus — held below bespoke ERP depth.
Shopify Checkout and Shop Pay are conversion strengths; plan-level processing rates improve on higher tiers.
Large app store plus native channel connectors (social, marketplaces) — ecosystem is a platform differentiator.
POS Lite on Basic and full POS on higher tiers support retail extensions — strong but not every merchant needs POS.
Plus, multi-location inventory, and automation (Flow) support high GMV brands — enterprise path is clear.
Headline plans are competitive but apps, themes, and processing spreads compress value on growing stores.
Shopify Magic / Sidekick ship native AI for merchandising and ops — useful, not the primary purchase driver.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine ecommerce editorial criteria using category weights (storefront/commerce fit 15, catalog/orders 14, ease 12, checkout 12, integrations 12, value 12, omnichannel/POS 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — SaaS platforms, open-source carts, omnichannel POS bundles, and dropshipping sourcing apps are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score; affiliate economics are excluded.
